questions: Should the function raise an error for an empty nested list (e.g., [[]]) or treat it as an empty flattened list and raise ValueError?
Are elements guaranteed to be numeric (int/float) or should non-numeric elements be handled (e.g., strings, None)?
Is the median calculation for even n using the average of the two middle values after sorting, as implied, or is there a different definition (e.g., lower middle)?
Should the function handle very large nested lists where recursion depth might exceed limits, or is recursion acceptable?
Are nested lists allowed to contain other iterable types (e.g., tuples, sets) besides lists?
Is the median required to be a float even for integer inputs (e.g., median of [1,2] should be 1.5 vs 1)?
Should the function preserve the order of elements during flattening (e.g., depth-first vs breadth-first) or is any flattening order acceptable as long as sorting is applied?
What should happen if the flattened list contains NaN or infinite values? Should they be handled specially?
